Hi Emma — thanks for the heads up and the screenshot. I see this occasionally: Calendly can default to the visitor's browser timezone and in some configurations the embedded link forces Pacific on us. Apologies for the confusion.

Quick options we can do right away:
- I can send a manual Google Calendar invite with explicit timezones (I find that avoids the browser-local conversion).
- I can also attach an ICS you can import that will show the correct times in your calendar.
- If you prefer the scheduling link, please click "View in your timezone" at the top of the Calendly page (sometimes hidden) or paste the link in a private window.

To unblock, does either of these work:
1) Oct 8, 07:00 PT / Oct 8, 15:00 BST / Oct 8, 23:00 JST — 30 mins (this hits Kai at a late but acceptable time)
2) Oct 8, 08:00 PT / Oct 8, 16:00 BST / Oct 9, 00:00 JST — 30 mins (one hour later for APAC)

I'm attaching a quick ICS for the first slot — redwood_demo_oct08_0700_pdt.ics — you can import it into Google/Outlook. If neither works, I can propose two separate demos (EU-focused + APAC-focused) and record one for the other region.

Let me know which you prefer and I'll send the invite.

Cheers,
Rishi Malhotra
